title: Ship one real delegation — and repair it
desc: Create a Cowork task, approve its tested steps, run it for real, correct it in Settings, and read a failure without guessing.
learningGoal: After this lesson you have one Cowork task that has really run, and you can turn a failure card into a fixed task without guessing.

steps.title: The chapter where you stop reading
steps.bodyMd:
Bart is a buyer at Van Dijk Groep. Every morning he re-reads supplier mail to work out what needs answering today: twenty minutes gone before he has started on anything of his own.

Reading about handing that over does not get it handed over. In this chapter you make one task of your own, approve its steps, run it for real while you watch, read what it did, and learn where a failure shows up and what to press.

Pick something **small, repeatable, and harmless if the first result is mediocre**, and let it send only to yourself. A first task does not have to impress anyone; it has to teach you where to look when the next one fails.

steps.title: Nothing here is permanent, except one button
steps.bodyMd:
Handing work to something that runs while you are not looking feels like losing control, so take the way back first.

- **Pause**, at the top of the task, stops it from starting; **Resume** puts it back. The task keeps its settings, its steps and its history.
- **Delete this task**, at the very bottom of the task's History, is the one-way door: *It stops for good, with its runs. This cannot be undone.*

You can have **10 tasks**. A paused task still counts; only deleting gives a place back. So make one now, and at the end of the chapter pause it if you might want it later, or delete it if you are sure you will not.

steps.title: What happens after you press Set up and test
steps.bodyMd:
1. The home shows your task's name with **Setting up the steps**, then **Testing once, nothing is sent**, then **Ready for your check**. The status reads **Testing** meanwhile.
2. Under **Needs you**: *The steps are ready and tested. Check them once.* Press **Open and approve**.
3. The task opens. Read **This is what you would have received**: the real output of the test. Press **Approve**, or **Change something** if it is not right.
4. Press **Run for real now** at the top. That run is real: it reads your data and sends to who is under Sends to.

If setting up does not work, a card says *Cowork could not set up the steps.* and lets you choose **Try setting up again** or **Let the AI work it out every run**. Until you choose, the task waits.

steps.title: Make it, approve it, run it: we check your real list
steps.instruction: Open Cowork, type one sentence for work you would genuinely hand over, and choose **Show what I understood**. Check the four lines and leave only **Me** under Sends to. Press **Set up and test** (or **Start**, where that is the button), approve the steps under Needs you, and press **Run for real now** on the task. The checklist reads your own task list: it wants a task that exists and one run for real; the test does not count. A task you made earlier counts too. Use the minimise button at the top of this lesson to tuck it away while you work.

steps.question: On Bart's new task, Run for real now is greyed out, and under it reads: "It cannot run for real yet: its steps wait for your approval." What gets him going?

choices.label: Approve the steps: Open and approve under Needs you, read what the test produced, then Approve.
Wait until 07:30 tomorrow; the schedule will start it anyway.
choices.feedback: The schedule is held back by the same rule. A task whose steps wait for approval skips its moments; nothing runs and nothing is sent.

choices.label: Delete the task and make it again from the chat instead.
choices.feedback: That throws the tested steps away for nothing. The button already says what it needs: one approval.

steps.explanation: A button that is off always says why under it. Here the why is the hold: the task runs for real only after you approved what its test produced.

steps.title: Reading the task after its first run
steps.bodyMd:
Open the task once the run is over.

- At the top: its latest result, *Done · Today 07:31*, with the result itself and **Next:** with its next moment. *Nothing to do · …* is a run that found nothing to do.
- **Steps**: *Fixed steps, the same on every run, top to bottom.* Each step says what it does: **Reads**, **Changes**, **Sends**, or **AI writes or decides**. **Test, sends nothing** tries them again on today's data.
- **History**: **Runs** (every run in plain words), **Changes** (every change to the task, with Restore for earlier approved steps) and **Proof of each run**.

The result also reached your notifications, under Cowork.

steps.question: The next morning Bart's task reads "Nothing to do · Today 07:30". There is no card under Needs you. What does that tell him?

choices.label: The run finished normally and found nothing to do, for example no new supplier mail.
The run failed quietly.
choices.feedback: A failure is never quiet: the task would read Failed and a card under Needs you would name the step and the cause, with one action.

choices.label: The run is still waiting for his approval.
choices.feedback: Then the word would be Needs you, with a card that asks him something. Nothing to do is a finished run.

steps.explanation: Nothing to do is a success with an empty answer. Only chase it if you expected output every time; then the sentence or the time is what needs changing.

steps.title: Correct it under Settings, not by starting over
steps.bodyMd:
There is no Edit button. Everything is under **Settings**, in the same four rows as the card, each with **Change**:

- **What**: the name, the sentence, and a **Target to track**.
- **When**: when it starts, how often, which days, at what time.
- **Uses**: the apps it may use and how it works.
- **Sends to**: who receives it, and the one **Ask me** choice.

Two things to know before you save:

- A name or a time is saved at once. A new sentence or other apps on a task with fixed steps is **Save and test**: Cowork rebuilds the steps, tests them once without sending, and you approve the changed steps before it runs again.
- Recipients are not changed here. To send to someone else, *say so in the sentence under What*.

steps.question: Bart is away for three weeks and does not want the daily digest piling up. Which move can he take back when he returns?

choices.label: Pause at the top of the task, then Resume when he is back.
Delete this task, and make it again in three weeks.
choices.feedback: The confirmation is blunt about it: it stops for good, with its runs, and this cannot be undone. He would also have to set up and approve the steps again.

choices.label: Under Settings → When, set How often to Once.
choices.feedback: That rewrites the schedule for good, and it would still run one more time. Pause is the switch made for this.

choices.label: Under Settings → Uses, switch every app off.
choices.feedback: The task would still run, just blind, and on a task with fixed steps other apps mean Save and test and a new approval. That is not a pause.

steps.explanation: Pause is the reversible control: nothing starts, the task keeps its steps, settings and history, and Resume puts it back. Delete this task is the only irreversible button.

steps.title: What a failure looks like
Four cards, four different moves
steps.instruction: Van Dijk Groep has four tasks with a card under Needs you on the same morning. Match what the card says to the button that resolves it.

pairs.note: The mailbox connection expired. Sign in again opens Settings → Connections, where your own credential lives. Then run it again; the sentence was never the problem.

pairs.left: "The steps are in the wrong order, so it cannot run."
pairs.note: Cowork can put the steps in the right order itself. What the task may read and send stays the same.

pairs.left: "Cowork could not set up the steps."
pairs.right: Try setting up again, or Let the AI work it out every run
pairs.note: Cowork never makes that second choice for you. Until you pick one, the task waits; the AI choice can be undone.

pairs.left: "The last run took too long and was stopped."
pairs.note: Nothing about the task itself is wrong, so the first move is simply another run.

steps.question: A card on Bart's task says "The sign-in of Outlook ran out." He opens Settings, and his admin also opens the admin dashboard on her own screen. Which screen does Bart need?

choices.label: Settings → Connections: the personal screen in his own Settings menu, where his own credential for the mailbox lives. The card's Sign in again goes there.
Admin dashboard → Security & access → Access → Grants.
choices.feedback: That admin screen decides who is allowed to use an integration; it never holds Bart's own credential. Even after a grant, Bart signs in to his own account under Settings → Connections.

choices.label: The task's Settings → Uses, under Apps it may use.
choices.feedback: That list decides which apps this one task may use. It cannot sign an expired account back in.

choices.label: Settings → Security.
choices.feedback: Security covers his own sign-in to Bee Flow, not the accounts Bee Flow connects out to. Those live under Connections.

steps.explanation: Settings → Connections is personal and holds your credentials; the admin's Grants decide who may connect at all. An expired sign-in is always the first one. Reconnecting also switches back on the tasks that paused themselves for it.

steps.title: Your turn: repair a task without starting over
steps.instruction: Bart's digest has run for two weeks. Two things are wrong: it should also go to inkoop@vandijk.nl, and it runs at 07:30 while he wants it at 07:00. Write, in three to five sentences, exactly what he does on the task page for each change: which row of Settings, what he changes, and what Cowork does next (saved at once, or Save and test with a new approval). Then say in one line what he checks after the next run to know it worked.
steps.placeholder: e.g. For the time he opens Settings → When, chooses Change and sets… That is saved at once. For the address he…

steps.title: What you can do now
steps.bodyMd:
You have a Cowork task that has really run, and a way back from anything it does next.

- **Get it running.** Set up and test, approve what the test produced, then Run for real now. A greyed-out button always says what it waits for.
- **Correct instead of delete.** Settings holds What, When, Uses and Sends to; a new sentence or other apps means Save and test and one more approval. Pause and Resume are the reversible pair.
- **Read the card before you act.** A failure is a card under Needs you with one action: Sign in again, Fix it for me, See what is wrong or Run it again. Nothing to do is not a failure.

If the task you just made was only practice, pause it, or delete it to get the place back.

ex-cowork-hands-on-repair.title: Repairing a task in Settings
ex-cowork-hands-on-repair.task: The learner describes how to make two changes to an existing Cowork task on its page: add a colleague's address as a recipient, and move the time from 07:30 to 07:00. For each: which Settings row, what is changed, and what Cowork does next. Then one line on what to check after the next run.
criteria: Moves the time under Settings → When (Change), and says it is saved at once without a new approval.

Adds the recipient by saying it in the sentence under Settings → What (Sends to itself cannot be edited on the task page), and says that a task with fixed steps then rebuilds and tests its steps (Save and test) and needs approving again.
Does not delete and recreate the task, and does not use Pause as a fix.
Names something concrete to check after the next run: the latest result at the top, History → Runs, a message waiting under Needs you for the colleague's copy, or the notification.
ex-cowork-hands-on-repair.guidance: Pass a plain, correct description even if informal. Do not pass an answer that edits recipients under Sends to directly, that looks for an Edit button, that deletes and recreates the task, or that claims the changed steps run without a new approval. Mentioning that the message to the colleague first waits under Needs you (Show me each message first) is a plus.

practiceTopic.title: Running, reading and repairing a Cowork task
practiceTopic.summary: How a new task gets from Set up and test to its first real run, how to read and correct it, and what each kind of failure card asks you to press.
facts: After Set up and test the home shows 'Setting up the steps', 'Testing once, nothing is sent' and 'Ready for your check', then a Needs you card 'The steps are ready and tested. Check them once.' with 'Open and approve'.
Run for real now is off while the steps wait for approval and says why under it: 'It cannot run for real yet: its steps wait for your approval.'; approving does not itself start a run.
The test of the steps and the approval do not count as a run; the task's first real run comes from Run for real now or from its schedule.

Pause and Resume are reversible; 'Delete this task' sits at the very bottom of History and its confirmation says it stops for good, with its runs, and cannot be undone. Each person can have 10 tasks, paused ones included.

There is no Edit screen: Settings holds What, When, Uses and Sends to; a name or a time saves at once, a new sentence or other apps on a task with fixed steps is 'Save and test' and needs a new approval.
Recipients cannot be edited on the task page; the Sends to row says to say it in the sentence under What.

A failure is always a card under Needs you that names the step and the cause, with one action such as Sign in again, Fix it for me, See what is wrong or Run it again; the raw error sits under Technical details.
An expired sign-in is repaired under Settings → Connections; reconnecting also resumes the tasks that paused themselves for it.
